tasks.short: Demonstrate the system to customers and explain false alarms.

steps.what: Read the panel manual on false alarm causes
Read the customers mail about false alarms
Read the installed systems on the work order
Draft the causes and consequences of false alarms

loop.purpose: Write a draft explanation of false-alarm causes from the manual section the installer already opened.
loop.input: Panel manual notes, customer mail notes, and the panel state.
loop.check: The draft names one cause, one consequence, and the manual section id. It does not judge whether the cause is the right one.
loop.stop: The draft is written. The loop does not wait for the installer.
loop.why_not_simpler: The manual is free text. A stored field on the work order does not hold an explanation of a false alarm.

steps.what: Demonstrate systems and explain the false alarm consequences
outputs: customer account of the false alarms

steps.what: Check the causes against what the customers saw
inputs: customer account of the false alarms

steps.what: Release the accepted explanation of the false alarms
outputs: work order holding the accepted false-alarm explanation v1

tasks.design: The installer still demonstrates the system to the customer at the panel. A bounded loop drafts the causes and consequences of false alarms from the panel manual in {DOCS} and the customer mail in {EMAIL}, and stops when that draft is written. The installer checks it against what the customers saw, then releases that accepted explanation onto the work order in {PROJECT} without rewriting it.
tasks.previous_blocker: The explanation sat in a manual the installer had to read at the panel, and a wrong cause can send people out of a building.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can draft from a manual section and a mail thread that the installer has already opened. The work order already holds the visit.
tasks.still_hard: Only the customer can say what they saw, and only the installer can judge whether that matches the cause.
tasks.human_edge: The installer still stands at the panel and decides which cause fits what the customers saw.
tasks.altitude: The demonstration stays the week. The installer gains a draft explanation to accept or reject, and still decides what to say at the panel.

reach.role: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment
reach.task: Separate a nuisance trip from a device fault before telling the customer.
reach.learn: Which cause is a false alarm and which is a failed device, before the explanation is released.

evidence.claim: The demonstration stays spoken at the panel. The draft is only a written account of causes and consequences from the panel manual and the customer mail. Model knowledge.

Dynamics 365 Field Service with Copilot writes recaps of work orders and can draft a work order from a customer email in Outlook. That supports drafting from customer mail only. It does not explain false alarms from a panel manual, and no time saving is taken from it.

Under WOR article 27(1)(l), a workflow system can be staff tracking and, without works council consent, may in principle not be used. This design adds no van location tracking. Consent is still in the build because the work-order draft records the visit.

assumptions: Largest remainder on the means prior gives screens 4, spreadsheets 1, mail 5, documents 11, meetings 79. The 0.9 spreadsheet prior is folded into documents, which become 12. Those figures are the same panel facts already in the manual. This is a design split, not a measured study.

Document time is split into reading the manual (6), drafting the explanation (3), checking it (2), and releasing it (1). Mail, the work-order screen, and the demonstration keep their prior shares and stay at remaining 100.

The work order stores the job and the panel. It does not store a false-alarm explanation. Producer of the manual text is the read of the manual; producer of the customer words is the demonstration. If the manual is not available as text, the draft is skipped and the installer speaks from the book.

The machine draft is not gated. Its loop stops when the draft is written. The check names accepted false-alarm explanation v1. The release commits that version and does not edit it. A later edit voids the check.

The spoken demonstration is not a record commit. The one-point release is the written note already inside today's document time. When the visit is spoken only, the saving is zero. Focal incremental hours are zero because the installer already reads the manual and already checks the explanation. The incremental entry is system time to keep manual section ids current. Existing work-order runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Whether this crew leaves a written explanation on the work order, or only speaks it at the panel.
Whether the works council has already consented to the work-order tool recording visits.
research_questions: On a typical visit, is the false-alarm explanation written down, or only spoken?
Which manual section do installers actually use for false alarms on the panels this crew fits?

already_counted.description: The installer still compares the draft causes with what the customers saw. Those hours sit in the check.

incremental.description: Keep the manual section ids the draft must cite current when a panel manual is reissued.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Net is 3, the draft share only. Low is 0 when the explanation is only spoken. High is 2 when the manual section is long and the installer still rewrites one cause after the visit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect the site and determine materials and procedures.

steps.what: Read the work order for this installation
Read mail about materials for this installation
Study the building plans and the installation manuals
Inspect the installation site against the building plans
Draft the materials requirements and installation procedures

loop.purpose: Write a draft of materials and procedures from the plans, the manuals, and the site findings.
loop.input: Job and panel type, materials mail notes, plan and manual notes, and site findings.
loop.check: Each line names a material, a quantity, and a manual section id. It does not judge whether the quantity fits the building.
loop.stop: The draft is written. The loop does not wait for the installer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Plans and manuals are free text, and the site findings are prose. The work order names the job and the panel; it does not hold quantities.

steps.what: Check the materials and procedures against the site
Release the accepted materials onto this installation order
outputs: work order holding the accepted materials list v1

tasks.design: The installer still inspects the site and still studies the building plans and the installation manuals in {DOCS}. After that, a bounded loop drafts the materials requirements and installation procedures from those notes and from the work order in {PROJECT}, and stops when the draft is written. The installer checks the quantities against the building, then releases that accepted list onto the work order without rewriting it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quantities live in plans and manuals, and the work order only names the job and the panel, so someone had to read both and tally them after walking the site.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can read plan text and manual text the installer has already opened, and the work order already holds the job.
tasks.still_hard: A drawing does not show a blocked riser. The installer still has to see the building.
tasks.human_edge: The installer still walks the site and decides whether a quantity fits the route that is actually there.
tasks.altitude: The site walk stays the week. The installer gains a materials draft to accept or reject, and still decides what the building needs.

reach.task: Read a cable route on a building plan before ordering cable.
reach.learn: Which route a materials list may assume, and which route the building does not have.

evidence.claim: The site walk stays physical. The draft only proposes materials from plans, manuals, and site findings. The work order is not assumed to store quantities. Model knowledge.

FieldBuddy completes work orders and technician checklists, and can turn a work order into an invoice. That is the class of record the accepted materials list is released onto. It is not cited as reading building plans, and no time saving is taken from it.

A DPIA is mandatory for systematic monitoring of employees, including GPS in vehicles. This design adds no location tracking. A workflow that records the visit still needs works council consent under WOR article 27(1)(l).

AI that allocates jobs on behaviour or traits, or monitors performance, is high-risk under annex III point 4(b), with duties from 2 December 2027. This design does not dispatch work or score the installer.

assumptions: Largest remainder on the means prior gives screens 3, spreadsheets 2, mail 2, documents 25, meetings 68. The two spreadsheet points stay on this task only: they are the materials tally the installer writes today. They are not a grid reused on the other tasks. Document points stay 25, split into studying plans and manuals (19), checking the list (3), and releasing it (3).

The inspection, the reads, the check, and the release stay at remaining 100. Only the tally drafting is machine. The work order stores job id, site address, and panel type, produced by the office that opened the job and read here. It does not store quantities. Producer of the plan text is the study step. Producer of site findings is the inspection. If a plan is not text, the installer types the list.
The machine draft is not gated. Its loop stops when the draft is written. The check names accepted materials list v1. The release commits that version onto the work order and does not edit it.

No van tracking is added. Focal incremental hours are zero: the installer already studies the plans and already checks the list. The incremental entry is system time to keep material codes current. Existing work-order runtime earns no labour saving. The code the procedures must follow is unknown and is not used as a saving.
unknowns: Whether the work order already stores material quantities, or only the job and the panel type.
Which national fire-alarm code this crew's procedures must follow.
Whether the works council has already consented to the work-order tool.
research_questions: After a site inspection, where does the materials tally live today, on the work order or in a separate tally?
Do the installation manuals this crew uses state quantities, or only the fitting method?

already_counted.description: The installer still checks the drafted quantities against the site findings. Those hours sit in the check.

incremental.description: Keep material codes the draft may cite current when the catalogue changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Net is 2, the tally draft only. Low is 0 when the building has no standard manual section and the installer writes the whole list. High is 1 when the manual states the quantities and the check still changes a line.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult clients on risks and security requirements.

steps.what: Read the clients mail about security risks
Read the installed security devices on the work order
Read earlier notes on these clients security risks
Consult clients to assess the security risks
Draft the security requirements from the clients risks

loop.purpose: Write a draft of security requirements from the risks the client stated in the consult.
loop.input: Client mail notes, installed device notes, earlier risk notes, and the client risk account.
loop.check: Each line is tied to a risk id that appears in the client risk account. It does not judge whether the risk is real.
loop.stop: The draft is written. The loop does not wait for the installer.
loop.why_not_simpler: The client risk account is free text from the consult. A fixed form cannot state a requirement the client has just described.

steps.what: Check each requirement against the clients risks
Release the accepted security requirements for these clients
outputs: opportunity holding the accepted security requirements v1

tasks.design: The installer still consults the client and still judges the risk in the room. A bounded loop then drafts security requirements from that conversation, the client mail in {EMAIL}, and the devices on the work order in {PROJECT}, and stops when the draft is written. The installer checks each requirement against the risk the client named, then releases that accepted version onto the opportunity without rewriting it.
tasks.previous_blocker: The risk is what the client says about the building, and a requirement written before that conversation misses the opening the client cares about.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can draft requirements from a conversation note and mail the installer has already captured. It cannot decide the risk.
tasks.still_hard: The client may understate a risk, and the installer is accountable for what gets written as a requirement.
tasks.human_edge: The installer still sits with the client and decides which risk becomes a requirement.
tasks.altitude: The consult stays the week. The installer gains a requirements draft to accept or reject, and still decides the risk.

reach.task: Describe an opening to a client before agreeing what must be secured.
reach.learn: How a security requirement stays tied to the door the client named.

evidence.claim: The consult and the risk judgement stay with the installer. The draft only proposes requirements from what the client said, the mail, and the devices already recorded. Model knowledge. No product in the digest is cited as assessing a client's risk.
Under WOR article 27(1)(l), a workflow system can be staff tracking and, without works council consent, may in principle not be used. This design adds no van location tracking.

AI that allocates jobs on behaviour or traits, or monitors performance, is high-risk under annex III point 4(b), with duties from 2 December 2027. This design does not dispatch work or score the installer.

assumptions: Largest remainder on the means prior gives screens 3, spreadsheets 2, mail 7, documents 16, meetings 72. Meetings take the tied 0.8 remainder because 71.8 is larger than the document 15.8, then documents, then mail. The 2.2 spreadsheet prior is folded into documents, which become 18. Risk notes are prose. This is a design split, not a measured study.

Document time is split into reading earlier notes (10), drafting requirements (4), checking them (2), and releasing them (2). The consult, the mail, and the device screen keep their shares and stay at remaining 100.

The client risk account is produced by the consult, not by the draft. The work order holds devices already installed, read before the consult. Requirements are not stored fields. If the consult is not written down, the draft is skipped.

The machine draft is not gated. Its loop stops when the draft is written. The check names accepted security requirements v1. The release commits that version and does not edit it. The live consult is not a record commit. Colleague talk is not involved; the client is outside the organisation.

Focal incremental hours are zero. The installer already reads the notes and already judges the requirements. The incremental entry is system time to keep requirement headings current. Existing work-order runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Whether security requirements are written after the consult, or only agreed in the room.
Whether the works council has already consented to the work-order tool.
research_questions: After a client consult, where do the agreed security requirements get written today?
Which risks does this crew refuse to turn into a requirement without a second visit?

already_counted.description: The installer still checks each drafted requirement against the risk the client named. Those hours sit in the check.

incremental.description: Keep the requirement headings the draft must use current when the crew's offer changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Net is 4, the requirements draft only. Low is 0 when the consult produces no written requirements. High is 3 when the mail and notes already hold most risks and the check still drops one line.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep informed of new products and developments.

steps.what: Read mail about new products and developments
Read documents on new products and developments
Read the supplier pages on these products
Hear the supplier briefing on these products
Draft what changed in these products and developments

loop.purpose: Write a draft of what changed in the products the installer has already read and heard about.
loop.input: Product mail notes, product document notes, supplier page notes, and briefing notes.
loop.check: Each line names a product and a change and points at a source line. It does not judge whether the change matters.
loop.stop: The draft is written. The loop does not wait for the installer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Product mail, manuals, and briefing notes are free text. No stored field holds what changed.

steps.what: Check each change against the product developments
Release the accepted change note on these products
outputs: product file holding the accepted product change note v1

tasks.design: The installer still reads product mail in {EMAIL}, documents in {DOCS}, and supplier pages on {PARTNER_PORTAL}, and still attends the supplier briefing. A bounded loop then drafts what changed in these products and developments, and stops when the draft is written. The installer checks that note against the developments, then releases the accepted note into {DOCS} for the crew without rewriting it.
tasks.previous_blocker: What changed is spread across mail, a manual, and a briefing, and the installer has to judge which change matters for the panels already installed.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded loop can draft a change note from text the installer has already opened. It cannot decide which change matters.
tasks.still_hard: A new product can be irrelevant to this crew's panels, and only the installer knows which sites would be affected.
tasks.human_edge: The installer still decides which product change matters for the panels this crew installs.
tasks.altitude: Reading and the supplier briefing stay the week. The installer gains a change note to accept or reject, and still decides what matters.

reach.task: Keep up with a new device model before the next installation.
reach.learn: Which product change affects an installation this crew already does, and which one does not.

evidence.claim: Reading product mail, documents, and a supplier briefing stays with the installer. No product in the digest watches product news. The draft is only a short note of what changed in text already opened. Model knowledge.

Under WOR article 27(1)(l), a workflow system can be staff tracking and, without works council consent, may in principle not be used. This design adds no van location tracking and does not score who read a product note.

assumptions: Largest remainder on the means prior gives screens 9, spreadsheets 1, mail 17, documents 24, meetings 49. Mail takes the tied 0.7 remainder because 16.7 is larger than screens 8.7, then screens, then meetings over the spreadsheet tie because 48.6 is larger than 1.6. The 1.6 spreadsheet prior is folded into documents, which become 25. Product news is not kept as a grid. This is a design split, not a measured study.

Document time is split into reading product documents (20), drafting the change note (2), checking it (2), and releasing it (1). Mail, supplier pages, and the briefing keep their shares and stay at remaining 100. The meeting share is treated as a supplier briefing, which is outside the organisation. A talk with a colleague would not use that authority.

No stored field holds what changed. Producers are the mail read, the document read, the supplier-page read, and the briefing. If the installer only reads and does not keep a note, the draft is skipped.

The machine draft is not gated. Its loop stops when the draft is written. The check names accepted product change note v1. The release commits that version into the product file and does not edit it. The release is internal, to a colleague, not a send outside the organisation.

Focal incremental hours are zero. The installer already reads and already judges the change. The incremental entry is system time to keep product document ids current. No product-news board is built. Existing portal runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Whether the installer already keeps a short note of product changes, or only reads and attends the briefing.
Whether the meeting time is a supplier briefing or an internal talk. An internal talk would not be an external action.
research_questions: Where, if anywhere, does this crew write down a product change after a supplier briefing?
Which product documents does the installer actually open in a month?

already_counted.description: The installer still checks each drafted change against the product developments. Those hours sit in the check.

incremental.description: Keep product document ids the draft must cite current when a maker reissues a manual.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Net is 2, the change-note draft only. Low is 0 when the installer only reads and attends the briefing. High is 1 when a manual states the change and the check still drops a line.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment: separate a false alarm cause from a device fault before it is written down.
